description: Structured template for policy problem definition and framing analysis

metadata.framework: Stone's Policy Paradox + Bardach's Problem Definition

issue_overview.issue_title: Brief title for the policy issue

observable_facts: Empirical, observable facts that establish the situation
affected_stakeholders: Groups or individuals affected by the situation
current_consequences: Observable and potential consequences of the situation

problem_statement.core_problem: Clear statement of what makes the situation problematic
violated_values: Values, expectations, or norms being violated
problem_statement.gap_description: Gap between current state and desired state
problem_statement.problem_significance: Why this problem matters and warrants attention

competing_framings.narrative: How this framing tells the story of the problem
competing_framings.problem_definition: How problem is defined under this framing
solutions_implied: What solutions this framing makes logical or visible
disadvantaged: Who is disadvantaged by this framing
competing_framings.responsibility_assigned: Who is responsible for fixing the problem under this framing
success_metrics: What would count as success under this framing

selected_framings: Primary framing(s) selected for this analysis
working_framings.framing_acknowledgment: Acknowledgment that multiple valid framings exist

primary_values: Core values implicated in this problem

outcomes: What would count as progress or success
measurement: How success would be recognized or measured

what_excluded: What this problem definition explicitly excludes
uncertainties: Uncertainties or ambiguities in the problem definition

formatting_rules: Avoid taking sides on contested questions
